The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in accurately segmenting Earth images even with imperfect polyline labels. This study contributes to the field of remote sensing and offers a promising solution for improving the segmentation of Earth images in various applications.

Medical image segmentation is a crucial task in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning. However, obtaining accurate pixel-level annotations for training deep learning models is time-consuming and expensive. In this paper, we propose a weakly supervised approach for medical image segmentation that leverages extreme points as weak annotations. We introduce a novel loss function that encourages the model to focus on the extreme points during training. We evaluate our approach on two publicly available medical image datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art weakly supervised methods. Our results demonstrate that our approach achieves competitive segmentation performance while significantly reducing the need for expensive pixel-level annotations. This work has the potential to accelerate the development of deep learning models for medical image segmentation by reducing the annotation burden on medical experts.

This academic paper titled "Going to Extremes: Weakly Supervised Medical Image Segmentation" presents a novel approach for weakly supervised medical image segmentation. The authors propose a method that leverages extreme points, which are points on the boundary of an object, to obtain semantic segmentation masks. By combining the information from extreme points with a weakly supervised learning framework, the authors achieve accurate segmentation results without the need for pixel-level annotations. The proposed method is evaluated on several medical imaging datasets and compared with existing weakly supervised segmentation methods. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed approach in medical image segmentation tasks. Overall, this paper introduces an innovative solution for weakly supervised medical image segmentation, which has the potential to significantly reduce the manual effort required for annotation and improve the efficiency in medical imaging analysis.

This paper presents LAMP, a framework for training large deep neural networks with automated model parallelism for image segmentation tasks. Image segmentation is a challenging problem in computer vision that involves partitioning an image into different regions or objects. Deep neural networks have shown promising results in image segmentation, but training large networks can be computationally expensive and memory-intensive. LAMP addresses these challenges by automatically partitioning the model across multiple GPUs, enabling efficient parallel training. The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of LAMP on various image segmentation datasets, achieving state-of-the-art performance while significantly reducing training time and memory requirements. The proposed framework provides a scalable solution for training large deep nets for image segmentation tasks.

This paper introduces LAMP, a framework for training large deep neural networks with automated model parallelism for image segmentation tasks. Traditional approaches for distributed training of deep nets suffer from limitations when scaling to large models and large datasets. LAMP addresses these issues by dynamically partitioning the model across multiple GPUs, automatically scheduling computation and communication, and minimizing memory consumption. Experimental results demonstrate that LAMP achieves high training efficiency with improved memory usage and scalability. The proposed framework significantly speeds up training time and reduces memory requirements while maintaining competitive performance on various image segmentation datasets. LAMP has the potential to advance the field of image segmentation and enable efficient training of deep neural networks on large-scale datasets.

This paper proposes a novel approach for object recognition using contour sparse representation with SDD (Shape Descriptor Distribution) features. The proposed method aims to address the limitations of existing object recognition techniques by leveraging the contour information of objects and incorporating SDD features. The contour information is extracted using the Canny edge detection algorithm, and the SDD features are computed based on the distribution of shape descriptors. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, achieving competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art methods. The proposed method shows promise for improving object recognition accuracy and robustness in various applications.

This paper introduces a new method for object recognition called Contour Sparse Representation with SDD Features. The proposed method combines contour information and Sparse Discriminative Dictionary (SDD) features to improve object recognition accuracy. The contour information is extracted using the Canny edge detector, and then the contour features are encoded using the proposed Contour Sparse Representation approach. The SDD features are computed by training a dictionary on the training set and then using it to represent the test set. The proposed method is evaluated on two benchmark datasets and compared against several state-of-the-art object recognition methods. The experimental results show that the proposed method achieves higher recognition accuracy and outperforms the existing methods. Overall, this paper provides a novel approach for object recognition that combines contour information and SDD features, leading to improved performance.

This paper presents a method for land use and land cover (LULC) segmentation of RGB satellite images using the Fully Convolutional Network (FCN-8) architecture. The FCN-8 model is trained on a large dataset of labeled satellite images to learn the mapping between input RGB images and their corresponding LULC classes. The proposed method achieves high accuracy in segmenting LULC classes such as urban areas, vegetation, water bodies, and bare land. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the FCN-8 model in accurately segmenting LULC classes in RGB satellite images, making it a promising approach for automated LULC mapping and analysis.

This academic paper presents a novel approach for land use and land cover (LULC) segmentation of RGB satellite images using a fully convolutional network (FCN-8). The proposed method utilizes the FCN-8 architecture, which leverages the power of deep learning to effectively classify different land use and land cover classes in RGB satellite imagery. The authors validate the performance of their approach by conducting experiments on a dataset consisting of RGB satellite images from various regions. The experimental results demonstrate that the FCN-8 model outperforms existing segmentation methods in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. The findings of this study highlight the potential of utilizing deep learning techniques for LULC segmentation tasks and provide a valuable contribution to the field of remote sensing and image analysis.

This paper presents a novel algorithm for image labeling using a neural Markovian multiresolution approach. The proposed algorithm leverages the power of neural networks to learn the underlying structure of images and combines it with a Markovian framework to capture the spatial dependencies between neighboring pixels. Additionally, the algorithm incorporates a multiresolution strategy to handle images of varying scales and resolutions. Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed algorithm compared to existing state-of-the-art methods. The algorithm shows promising potential for applications in image segmentation, object recognition, and scene understanding.

This paper presents a new algorithm for image labeling, based on a neural Markovian multiresolution approach. The algorithm utilizes a combination of deep neural networks and Markov random fields to label images with high accuracy and efficiency. The multiresolution aspect of the algorithm allows for the integration of information at different scales, enabling the algorithm to capture both global and local image features. Experimental results on various image datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in achieving state-of-the-art image labeling performance. The algorithm has the potential to be applied in various computer vision applications, such as object recognition and scene understanding.

This paper explores the concept of learning to pay attention to mistakes and its impact on cognitive processes and performance. The authors argue that individuals who are able to effectively recognize and learn from their mistakes are more likely to improve their performance and achieve better outcomes. The paper reviews existing literature on the topic and presents empirical evidence from various studies to support this claim. Additionally, the authors discuss the potential mechanisms through which learning from mistakes occurs, including attentional processes and metacognitive strategies. The paper concludes by highlighting the implications of these findings for educational and professional settings, suggesting that promoting a culture of learning from mistakes can enhance individual and organizational performance.

This paper investigates the process of learning to pay attention to mistakes. It reviews the existing literature on error-related negativity (ERN) and error positivity (Pe) markers, which are neural signals associated with the detection of errors. The paper presents a study that examined how ERN and Pe markers changed over time as participants learned to pay attention to their mistakes during a cognitive task. The results showed that participants who received feedback on their errors showed increased ERN and Pe amplitudes, indicating improved error detection. Furthermore, the study found that attention to mistakes was associated with enhanced post-error accuracy and decreased subsequent errors. The findings suggest that individuals can learn to allocate attention to their mistakes, leading to more accurate performance and reduced errors. The implications of these findings for improving learning and performance are discussed.

This paper presents a comprehensive review of state-of-the-art fuzzy active contour models for image segmentation. Image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision and has numerous applications in various fields. Fuzzy active contour models are a popular approach for image segmentation due to their ability to handle complex and ambiguous image data. The paper provides an overview of the basic concepts and principles of fuzzy active contour models, including the use of fuzzy sets and fuzzy logic in the segmentation process. It then reviews several recent advancements in fuzzy active contour models, including the incorporation of spatial information, texture information, and shape priors. The paper also discusses the evaluation metrics used to assess the performance of fuzzy active contour models and provides a comparative analysis of different models based on these metrics. Finally, the paper concludes with a discussion on the challenges and future directions in the field of fuzzy active contour models for image segmentation. Overall, this paper serves as a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners interested in the latest developments in fuzzy active contour models for image segmentation.

This paper presents a review of state-of-the-art fuzzy active contour models for image segmentation. Image segmentation is an essential task in computer vision and has been widely studied over the years. Fuzzy active contour models incorporate fuzzy logic into traditional active contour models to improve their performance. This paper provides an overview of different fuzzy active contour models and compares their strengths and weaknesses. The review is based on a thorough analysis of recent literature in the field. The findings of this paper can guide researchers in selecting the most suitable fuzzy active contour model for their specific image segmentation task.

This paper presents a novel approach for segmenting greenhouses on high-resolution optical satellite imagery using deep learning techniques. The proposed method utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture to automatically learn and extract relevant features from the input images. The CNN is trained on a large dataset of labeled greenhouse images, enabling it to accurately classify pixels as either greenhouse or non-greenhouse. The performance of the proposed method is evaluated on a test dataset, and the results demonstrate its effectiveness in accurately segmenting greenhouses. The proposed approach offers a promising solution for automating the process of greenhouse segmentation, which can have various applications in agriculture, urban planning, and environmental monitoring.

This paper presents a novel approach for segmenting greenhouses on high-resolution optical satellite imagery using deep learning techniques. The proposed method combines convolutional neural networks and semantic segmentation to accurately identify and delineate greenhouses from the background. The process involves training a deep learning model on a large dataset of annotated images, using a combination of image augmentations and transfer learning to improve performance. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing techniques in terms of accuracy and efficiency. The findings of this study have significant implications for monitoring and managing greenhouse agriculture, enabling more effective resource allocation and enhanced decision-making in this domain.

This paper presents a novel approach for unsupervised learning of image segmentation based on differentiable feature clustering. The proposed method leverages the power of deep neural networks to learn meaningful representations of image features and then applies a clustering algorithm to group similar features together. The key contribution of this work is the introduction of a differentiable clustering loss function that allows end-to-end training of the segmentation model. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in achieving accurate and robust image segmentation without the need for manual annotations. The proposed approach has the potential to significantly advance the field of unsupervised image segmentation and has implications for various applications in computer vision and image analysis.

In recent years, deep learning has made significant progress in image segmentation tasks. However, most existing methods require large amounts of labeled data for training, which can be expensive and time-consuming to obtain. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel unsupervised learning approach for image segmentation based on differentiable feature clustering. The proposed method leverages the power of clustering techniques to group similar image features together, while also incorporating a differentiable loss function to optimize the clustering process. The experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach achieves competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art supervised methods, while requiring no prior labeling. Furthermore, we also evaluate the robustness of our method to diverse image properties and show its flexibility in handling various image segmentation scenarios. Overall, our work provides a promising direction for unsupervised learning of image segmentation, which can significantly reduce the annotation effort and enable practical applications in domains with limited labeled data.

This paper proposes a novel approach for medical image segmentation using superpixel-guided label softening. The traditional approach of directly assigning hard labels to pixels can lead to inaccurate segmentation results, especially in the presence of noise and artifacts. To address this issue, the authors introduce a superpixel-guided label softening technique that incorporates the spatial information provided by superpixels to improve the accuracy of segmentation. The proposed method first generates superpixels from the input image and then assigns soft labels to the pixels within each superpixel based on their similarity to the superpixel centroid. Experimental results on a dataset of medical images demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness to noise and artifacts. The findings of this study have the potential to enhance the performance of medical image segmentation algorithms and improve the diagnosis and treatment of various medical conditions.

This paper presents a novel approach for medical image segmentation called superpixel-guided label softening. The proposed method utilizes the concept of superpixels to group the pixels in an image, allowing for more efficient and effective segmentation. The technique involves using a softening function to smooth the transition between different label regions within a superpixel, resulting in more accurate and natural segmentation boundaries. The superpixel-guided label softening method is compared with several state-of-the-art segmentation algorithms on a variety of medical image datasets, demonstrating its superiority in terms of both segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. The results suggest that this approach has great potential for improving medical image segmentation and has practical applications in clinical settings.

Medical image segmentation is a critical task in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning. However, the privacy and security of medical data pose significant challenges in developing accurate and reliable segmentation algorithms. In this paper, we propose BUNET, a blind medical image segmentation method based on secure UNET. BUNET leverages the UNET architecture for accurate segmentation while incorporating privacy-preserving techniques to ensure the confidentiality of sensitive medical data. We evaluate the performance of BUNET on a dataset of medical images and compare it with existing segmentation methods. The results demonstrate that BUNET achieves competitive segmentation accuracy while maintaining the privacy and security of medical data. Our proposed method has the potential to enhance the development of secure and reliable medical image segmentation algorithms.

Medical image segmentation is an essential step in many clinical applications. However, due to privacy concerns and the sensitive nature of medical data, there is a need for secure segmentation methods that do not require the transmission or storage of raw medical images. In this paper, we propose BUNET, a blind medical image segmentation method based on the secure UNET architecture. BUNET utilizes encryption techniques to transform raw medical images into encrypted feature maps, which are then processed by the segmentation network without ever being decrypted. We evaluate BUNET on a dataset of medical images and compare its performance with other state-of-the-art segmentation methods. The experimental results demonstrate that BUNET achieves comparable segmentation accuracy while preserving the privacy of medical data. The proposed method shows promise in enabling secure medical image segmentation for clinical applications.

Superpixel segmentation is an important step in many computer vision applications. In this paper, we propose a novel superpixel segmentation algorithm using dynamic and iterative spanning forest. The algorithm starts by constructing an initial spanning forest based on the image gradient. Then, it iteratively updates the forest by merging and splitting the superpixels based on the local image information. The proposed algorithm achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of both boundary adherence and compactness. Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed algorithm compared to existing methods.

Superpixel segmentation is an essential preprocessing step for various computer vision tasks, such as object detection and semantic segmentation. This paper proposes a new approach for superpixel segmentation called Dynamic and Iterative Spanning Forest (DISF). Unlike previous methods, DISF dynamically generates superpixels by iteratively merging and splitting regions based on a local connectivity measure. This approach allows for better adaptation to image complexity and preserves finer details compared to existing methods. Experimental results on five benchmark datasets show that DISF outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of both boundary adherence and computational efficiency. Overall, DISF provides a more flexible and efficient solution for superpixel segmentation, making it a valuable tool for various computer vision applications.

This paper presents a new approach for interactive image segmentation using complex network construction based on particle competition and cooperation. The proposed method aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of image segmentation by leveraging the power of complex networks. The approach involves representing an image as a graph, where each pixel is a node and the relationships between pixels are represented by edges. The construction of the complex network is achieved through a particle competition and cooperation algorithm, which assigns weights to the edges based on the similarity between pixels. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. The findings of this study contribute to the field of interactive image segmentation and provide a new perspective on the use of complex networks in computer vision tasks.

This academic paper proposes a new approach for constructing complex networks for interactive image segmentation using particle competition and cooperation. The authors employ a new algorithm that combines particle competition and cooperation to iteratively optimize the network construction process. The proposed approach is evaluated using multiple benchmark datasets and compared with existing methods. Results show that the proposed approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. The paper concludes by discussing potential applications and future directions for this novel approach in the field of interactive image segmentation.

This paper presents a novel approach for automated pavement crack segmentation using a U-Net-based convolutional neural network (CNN). Pavement crack segmentation is a crucial task in road maintenance and inspection, as it helps in identifying and assessing the severity of cracks. The proposed method utilizes a U-Net architecture, which has been proven effective in various image segmentation tasks. The CNN is trained on a large dataset of pavement crack images, and the resulting model is capable of accurately segmenting cracks from input images. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, achieving high accuracy and efficiency in pavement crack segmentation. The automated system can potentially assist road maintenance and inspection teams in identifying and prioritizing areas that require repair or maintenance.

Pavement crack detection is a crucial task in the field of infrastructure management. It is typically performed manually by human experts, leading to time-consuming and costly processes. This paper proposes an automated approach for pavement crack segmentation using a U-Net-based convolutional neural network. The U-Net architecture is well-suited for this task due to its ability to effectively capture contextual information and perform accurate segmentation. The dataset used in this study consists of high-resolution pavement images with annotated crack regions. The proposed method achieves excellent results with high accuracy and precision in segmenting pavement cracks. Additionally, the approach is computationally efficient and can be easily applied to large-scale real-world datasets. This automated crack segmentation technique has the potential to significantly improve the efficiency and accuracy of pavement maintenance and management processes.

Automated image segmentation is a crucial task in computer vision and has numerous applications in various fields. In this paper, we propose a deep learning approach for automated image segmentation that combines region, edge, and contour models into a unified framework. Our method utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture to learn and extract features from the input images. We then employ a multi-task learning strategy to simultaneously train the region, edge, and contour models. The proposed approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness and robustness. Furthermore, we conduct extensive experiments and analysis to provide insights into the learned representations and the impact of different components in our model. Overall, our work contributes to the advancement of automated image segmentation techniques and provides a comprehensive framework for integrating region, edge, and contour models using deep learning.

This paper presents a deep learning approach for automated image segmentation using unified region, edge, and contour models. The proposed method leverages convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to learn highly representative features from image data and combines region, edge, and contour information to achieve accurate segmentation results. The authors perform extensive experiments on benchmark datasets and demonstrate that their approach outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. These findings suggest that the proposed deep learning framework has the potential to greatly improve automated image segmentation tasks in various domains.

This paper proposes a method for learning pose variations within a shape population using constrained mixtures of factor analyzers. The method aims to capture the underlying structure of the shape population by modeling the pose variations as a mixture of factor analyzers. The proposed method incorporates constraints on the factor analyzers to ensure that the learned pose variations are consistent with the observed data. Experimental results on a dataset of human body shapes demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in capturing and modeling pose variations within a shape population. The findings of this study have implications for various applications such as computer vision, robotics, and human-computer interaction.

This academic paper proposes a method for learning and representing the variations in pose within a shape population. The authors introduce a novel approach called constrained mixtures of factor analyzers, which can model the pose variations by capturing both the global shape information and the local deformation effects. The proposed method also incorporates constraints to ensure that the learned pose variations are plausible. The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their method through experiments on several shape datasets, showing that it can accurately capture and represent the pose variations within the shape population. The results of the experiments suggest that the proposed method can be a valuable tool for shape analysis and recognition tasks.

This paper presents ACNN, a full resolution deep convolutional neural network (DCNN) for medical image segmentation. ACNN is designed to address the challenges of segmenting medical images with high resolution and complex structures. The network architecture consists of multiple convolutional layers followed by upsampling layers to preserve the full resolution of the input image. ACNN also incorporates skip connections to enable information flow between different levels of the network. The proposed network is trained using a combination of pixel-wise cross-entropy loss and Dice loss. Experimental results on various medical image datasets demonstrate that ACNN achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. The proposed network has the potential to improve the accuracy and efficiency of medical image segmentation tasks, which can benefit various clinical applications.

Medical image segmentation is a crucial problem in computer vision that involves separating different structures or regions of interest in medical images. Deep convolutional neural networks (DCNNs) have shown great potential for this task, but most existing approaches only operate at low resolutions due to computational constraints. In this paper, we propose ACNN, a full-resolution DCNN architecture for medical image segmentation. ACNN employs a novel adaptive pooling layer and a hybrid loss function to effectively handle high-resolution medical images. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on two public medical image segmentation datasets and achieve competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art methods. Our results suggest that ACNN can serve as a powerful tool for accurately segmenting medical images at their full resolution.

This paper presents a deep learning-based automated image segmentation method for concrete petrographic analysis. Concrete petrography is a critical task in civil engineering, as it involves the identification and characterization of various components in concrete samples. Traditional manual methods for image segmentation in concrete petrography are time-consuming and subjective. In this study, we propose a deep learning approach using a convolutional neural network (CNN) to automatically segment concrete images into different components. The proposed method is trained on a large dataset of annotated concrete images and achieves high accuracy in segmenting various components such as aggregates, cement paste, and air voids. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms traditional manual methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. The proposed deep learning-based automated image segmentation method has the potential to significantly improve the efficiency and accuracy of concrete petrographic analysis in civil engineering applications.

Image segmentation is a critical step in concrete petrographic analysis, where different grains and pores need to be accurately identified and delineated. Traditional methods of image segmentation require manual intervention and are time-consuming and error-prone. In this paper, we propose a deep learning-based automated image segmentation approach for concrete petrographic analysis. We train a convolutional neural network (CNN) using a large dataset of concrete images, and then use the trained model to segment the images into different regions of interest. We evaluate the performance of our approach using a set of test images, and compare it with other state-of-the-art image segmentation techniques. The results show that our approach outperforms the traditional methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. This research contributes to the field of concrete petrographic analysis by providing a novel and effective automated image segmentation technique that can significantly improve the efficiency and accuracy of the analysis process.

This paper proposes a multi-task deep learning approach for image segmentation using recursive approximation tasks. The authors introduce a novel framework that leverages the power of deep learning to perform image segmentation tasks by recursively approximating the ground truth segmentation masks. The proposed method is able to learn from multiple tasks simultaneously, leading to improved segmentation performance. Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach compared to state-of-the-art methods. The authors also provide insights into the inner workings of the proposed framework and discuss potential future directions for research in this area.

This paper presents a multi-task deep learning approach for image segmentation by utilizing recursive approximation tasks. The proposed method leverages the ability of deep neural networks to learn multiple tasks simultaneously, and enhances it with recursive approximation tasks to improve segmentation accuracy. The Recursive Approximation Network (RAN) is developed, which consists of multiple subnetworks, each responsible for a specific approximation task. The subnetworks are trained jointly with the main segmentation task, facilitating the transfer of knowledge across tasks and enhancing the overall performance. Experimental results on benchmark datasets show that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art segmentation methods in terms of accuracy and robustness. The effectiveness of the recursive approximation tasks is demonstrated through ablation studies and analysis of learned representations. Overall, this work highlights the potential of multi-task deep learning and recursive approximation tasks for image segmentation tasks.

This paper proposes a novel self-ensembling model for semi-supervised medical image segmentation. The model leverages the consistency regularization framework to enforce transformation consistency between augmented versions of the same input image. This approach improves the robustness and generalization of the segmentation model by reducing the impact of data augmentation on the final segmentation results. Experimental results on a publicly available medical image dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed model, achieving state-of-the-art performance in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness. The proposed model has the potential to enhance the accuracy and reliability of medical image segmentation tasks, leading to improved clinical decision-making and patient care.

In the field of medical image segmentation, the limited availability of annotated data poses a challenge for accurate and robust segmentation algorithms. Semi-supervised learning methods have recently gained attention as they can leverage both labeled and unlabeled data to improve segmentation performance. In this paper, we propose a novel transformation consistent self-ensembling model for semi-supervised medical image segmentation. Our model integrates a transformation consistent loss term, which encourages the model to produce consistent segmentations under different transformations. We evaluate our approach on a large dataset of medical images and compare it with state-of-the-art methods. Our experiments show that the proposed model achieves significantly better segmentation performance compared to existing approaches, demonstrating its potential for improving accuracy and robustness in medical image segmentation tasks.

Few-shot image segmentation is a challenging task that requires the ability to segment objects in images with only a few annotated examples. In this paper, we propose SimPropNet, an improved similarity propagation method for few-shot image segmentation. SimPropNet leverages the power of deep neural networks to learn a similarity metric between pixels in the image and propagate the segmentation labels from the annotated examples to the unlabeled pixels. We introduce a novel similarity propagation module that incorporates both local and global context information to improve the accuracy of the segmentation. We evaluate SimPropNet on several benchmark datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art few-shot segmentation methods. The experimental results demonstrate that SimPropNet achieves superior performance in terms of both accuracy and efficiency. Our method shows great potential for practical applications in the field of image segmentation.

Few-shot image segmentation is a challenging task that aims to segment objects in images given only a few annotated examples. Existing methods typically rely on similarity propagation to overcome the lack of annotated data. However, these methods often suffer from the issues of limited context information and noisy similarity estimation. In this paper, we propose a novel similarity propagation network, called SimPropNet, which improves upon existing methods by leveraging contextual information and incorporating consistency constraints. Specifically, our approach employs the region-based context propagation module to enhance the context information and refine the similarity maps. Additionally, we introduce the consistency-guided propagation module to enforce consistency among different propagated results. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our SimPropNet achieves superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods in few-shot image segmentation.

This paper proposes a spatially constrained deep convolutional neural network (CNN) for nerve fiber segmentation in corneal confocal microscopic images. The aim is to address the challenge of inaccurate annotations in the training data, which can lead to poor segmentation performance. The proposed method incorporates a spatial constraint into the CNN architecture to improve the accuracy of nerve fiber segmentation. Experimental results on a dataset of corneal confocal microscopic images demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of segmentation accuracy, especially when dealing with inaccurate annotations. The findings of this study have implications for improving the reliability and efficiency of nerve fiber segmentation in corneal confocal microscopic images, which can aid in the diagnosis and monitoring of various ocular diseases.

Nerve fiber segmentation in corneal confocal microscopic images is a significant task in diagnosing various ocular diseases. Deep learning models have shown promising results in this domain, but their effectiveness heavily relies on accurate annotations, which are time-consuming and costly to obtain. In this paper, we propose a novel spatially constrained deep convolutional neural network (SC-DCNN) that leverages inaccurate annotations for nerve fiber segmentation. Our model incorporates a spatial regularization term to encourage spatial coherence in the predicted masks. We train and evaluate our SC-DCNN on a large dataset of corneal confocal microscopic images with both accurate and inaccurate annotations. Our results demonstrate that the proposed SC-DCNN outperforms existing deep learning models in terms of segmentation accuracy, even when trained on datasets with inaccurate annotations. This suggests the potential of our approach in reducing the annotation burden and making nerve fiber segmentation more accessible in clinical practice.

This paper proposes a novel approach for panoptic image segmentation and the task of splitting unfamiliar objects into parts. The proposed method utilizes a Generator Evaluator-Selector Net (GES-Net) that combines the strengths of generative models, evaluative models, and selective models. The GES-Net is trained in a two-step process, where the generator first generates potential object proposals, and the evaluator then evaluates the quality of these proposals. The selector then selects the most accurate proposals and splits them into parts. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed GES-Net in achieving state-of-the-art performance in both panoptic image segmentation and object splitting tasks. The proposed method has the potential to advance the field of computer vision and contribute to various applications such as object recognition and scene understanding.

This paper introduces a new framework called the Generator Evaluator-Selector Net (GESNet) for panoptic image segmentation and the task of splitting unfamiliar objects into their constituent parts. GESNet consists of three modules: a generator module that generates segment-level and part-level candidate proposals, an evaluator module that assigns scores to the proposals based on their quality, and a selector module that selects the best proposals for generating the final segmentation. The proposed GESNet is evaluated on various benchmark datasets and the results demonstrate its effectiveness in panoptic image segmentation and part splitting tasks compared to existing methods. The proposed framework provides a novel approach for solving these challenging tasks and has the potential for applications in various computer vision and image understanding tasks.

This paper presents a real-time high-performance semantic image segmentation method for urban street scenes. The proposed method utilizes a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture to achieve accurate and efficient segmentation results. The network is trained on a large-scale dataset of street scene images with pixel-level annotations. The method incorporates several key techniques, including dilated convolutions, atrous spatial pyramid pooling, and skip connections, to improve the segmentation performance. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy and speed. The method achieves real-time performance on a standard GPU, making it suitable for various applications such as autonomous driving and urban planning.

This paper presents a novel approach to real-time high-performance semantic image segmentation of urban street scenes. The proposed method utilizes a deep convolutional neural network architecture that combines the advantages of both fully convolutional networks and residual networks. The model achieves state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets and is able to process images in real time. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed approach, making it suitable for applications requiring real-time semantic image segmentation of urban street scenes, such as autonomous driving and traffic surveillance.

This paper presents a weakly-supervised multi-class semantic segmentation method for Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) radar data. The proposed method, called RSS-Net, leverages the rich spatial and temporal information provided by FMCW radar to perform semantic segmentation without the need for pixel-level annotations. RSS-Net consists of two main components: a radar signal processing module and a segmentation network. The radar signal processing module extracts features from the raw radar data, while the segmentation network utilizes these features to perform semantic segmentation. To train RSS-Net, a weak supervision strategy is employed, where only image-level labels are used. Experimental results on a publicly available FMCW radar dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of RSS-Net in accurately segmenting multiple classes in radar data. The proposed method achieves competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art weakly-supervised and fully-supervised semantic segmentation methods. Overall, RSS-Net provides a promising approach for multi-class semantic segmentation in FMCW radar data without the need for pixel-level annotations.

This paper presents RSS-Net, a weakly-supervised multi-class semantic segmentation method using Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) radar data. While radar sensors have been widely used in autonomous driving for object detection and tracking, their potential for detailed semantic segmentation is still underexplored. The proposed RSS-Net framework leverages a weakly-supervised learning approach to train a segmentation network using only image-level class labels. It incorporates a radar-driven attention mechanism to enhance the discriminative power of the network in differentiating object classes. Experimental results on a publicly available radar dataset demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed method in accurately segmenting multiple object classes, outperforming state-of-the-art weakly-supervised and radar-based segmentation techniques. The paper also discusses the challenges and future directions of integrating FMCW radar data into the semantic segmentation pipeline for autonomous driving applications.

Lane detection is a critical task in autonomous driving systems, as it provides crucial information for vehicle control and navigation. Existing methods for 3D lane detection often suffer from limited generalization and scalability, as they are designed for specific scenarios or require extensive manual annotation. In this paper, we propose Gen-LaneNet, a novel approach for 3D lane detection that is both generalized and scalable. Gen-LaneNet leverages a deep neural network architecture that can be trained on diverse datasets without the need for extensive manual annotation. We demonstrate the effectiveness of Gen-LaneNet on various challenging scenarios and show that it outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and robustness. Our approach has the potential to significantly improve the performance and scalability of 3D lane detection systems in autonomous driving applications.

Lane detection is an essential task for autonomous vehicles, enabling them to navigate safely on the road. In this paper, we propose a novel approach called Gen-LaneNet for 3D lane detection. Our method utilizes a deep neural network that decouples the task of lane segmentation and regression, allowing for a more flexible and scalable solution. By incorporating a range of anchor-based and anchor-free detection schemes, Gen-LaneNet achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmark datasets. Our experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and generalizability of our approach, making it a promising method for real-world applications of autonomous driving.

Out-of-distribution (OOD) detection is an important task in machine learning, as it helps identify samples that do not belong to any known classes. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for OOD detection in multi-label datasets using the latent space of a β-variational autoencoder (β-VAE). We first train a β-VAE on the multi-label dataset and then use the learned latent space to detect OOD samples. We introduce a novel OOD score based on the reconstruction error and the KL-divergence between the latent space of the β-VAE and a reference distribution. We evaluate our approach on several benchmark datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art methods. The experimental results show that our method achieves superior performance in OOD detection, outperforming existing approaches. Furthermore, we conduct ablation studies to analyze the impact of different components of our method. Overall, our proposed approach demonstrates the effectiveness of using the latent space of a β-VAE for OOD detection in multi-label datasets.

In this paper, we propose a method for out-of-distribution detection in multi-label datasets using the latent space of a β-VAE. Out-of-distribution samples are often challenging to detect in multi-label datasets due to the presence of multiple labels. By leveraging the latent space of the β-VAE, we are able to capture the distribution of in-distribution samples and estimate the probability of a sample being out-of-distribution. We evaluate our method on various multi-label datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art techniques. Our results show that our proposed method achieves superior performance in detecting out-of-distribution samples in multi-label datasets. Additionally, we provide insights into the behavior of the β-VAE latent space and discuss its implications for out-of-distribution detection in multi-label datasets.

This paper presents a novel approach for semi-supervised semantic image segmentation using self-correcting networks. The proposed method leverages both labeled and unlabeled data to improve the accuracy of segmentation results. The self-correcting network consists of two components: a segmentation network and a correction network. The segmentation network generates initial segmentation masks, while the correction network refines these masks by iteratively updating them based on the unlabeled data. The correction network learns to correct the errors made by the segmentation network, leading to improved segmentation results. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing semi-supervised segmentation methods in terms of accuracy and robustness. The self-correcting network approach shows promise for improving the performance of semantic image segmentation tasks.

This paper presents a novel approach to semi-supervised semantic image segmentation using self-correcting networks. Traditional semi-supervised methods often rely on pre-defined models or external datasets for guidance, limiting their applicability to new domains. In contrast, the proposed approach leverages the inherent structure of the image data to improve segmentation accuracy. The self-correcting network architecture is designed to iteratively refine segmentation results by adjusting internal representations based on uncertainty estimates. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and generalization to unseen data. These findings highlight the potential of self-correcting networks as a promising framework for semi-supervised semantic image segmentation.

Brain tumor segmentation is a critical task in medical image analysis, as it plays a crucial role in diagnosis and treatment planning. However, accurate and robust segmentation remains challenging due to the complexity and heterogeneity of brain tumors. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for robust multimodal brain tumor segmentation. Our method leverages feature disentanglement and gated fusion to effectively integrate information from multiple modalities, including T1-weighted, T1-weighted contrast-enhanced, T2-weighted, and fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) images. We first disentangle the features of each modality using a disentanglement module, which helps to capture modality-specific information. Then, we employ a gated fusion module to selectively combine the disentangled features, allowing the network to adaptively fuse information from different modalities. Experimental results on a publicly available brain tumor segmentation dataset demonstrate that our proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness. Our method also achieves competitive performance on a challenging dataset with a large number of brain tumor subtypes. Overall, our approach shows promise for improving the accuracy and robustness of brain tumor segmentation, which can have a significant impact on clinical decision-making and patient outcomes.

Brain tumor segmentation plays a crucial role in the diagnosis and treatment planning for patients. However, accurate and robust segmentation remains a challenging task due to the complexity and heterogeneity of brain tumors. In this paper, we propose a novel approach called Robust Multimodal Brain Tumor Segmentation via Feature Disentanglement and Gated Fusion. Our method leverages both the spatial and multimodal information of the brain images to improve segmentation accuracy. Specifically, we extract rich features from different imaging modalities using a deep convolutional neural network. Then, we disentangle the learned features into domain-specific and shared components to capture the specific characteristics of each modality and the common information across modalities. Finally, a gated fusion module is employed to leverage the disentangled features and generate the final segmentation map. Experimental results on a large publicly available dataset demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of our proposed approach, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness to noise and artifacts. Our method has the potential to contribute to more accurate and reliable brain tumor segmentation in clinical practice.

PointRend is a novel approach to image segmentation that treats the task as a rendering problem. Traditional segmentation methods typically assign a single label to each pixel, which can result in inaccurate boundaries and loss of fine-grained details. In contrast, PointRend leverages a set of randomly sampled points within each object instance to generate high-resolution masks. These points are then used to render the final segmentation mask, resulting in improved boundary quality and preservation of fine details. Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate that PointRend outperforms state-of-the-art segmentation methods in terms of both accuracy and visual quality. Additionally, PointRend is computationally efficient and can be easily integrated into existing segmentation pipelines. Overall, this work presents a promising approach to image segmentation that bridges the gap between traditional pixel-wise methods and rendering-based techniques.

PointRend is a novel approach for image segmentation that formulates the problem as a rendering task. Unlike traditional segmentation methods that operate on the entire image, PointRend selectively samples a sparse set of points in the image, renders them, and uses the rendered masks to estimate the segmentation masks. This reduces the computational cost and memory requirements, allowing PointRend to be applied efficiently on high-resolution images. The proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets for both instance and semantic segmentation tasks, demonstrating its effectiveness in improving segmentation accuracy.

Liver segmentation is an important task in medical image analysis, as it plays a crucial role in various clinical applications. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for liver segmentation in abdominal CT images using an auto-context neural network and self-supervised contour attention. The auto-context neural network is designed to capture the contextual information of the liver region, while the self-supervised contour attention mechanism helps to refine the segmentation results by focusing on the liver boundary. Experimental results on a publicly available dataset demonstrate that our proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of accuracy and robustness. The proposed approach has the potential to improve the efficiency and accuracy of liver segmentation in clinical practice, thereby facilitating the diagnosis and treatment of liver diseases.

Liver segmentation in abdominal CT images is an essential task in medical image analysis. In this paper, we propose a novel method for liver segmentation using an auto-context neural network and self-supervised contour attention. The auto-context neural network combines the outputs of multiple neural networks to improve the accuracy of liver segmentation. Additionally, the self-supervised contour attention mechanism focuses on the liver boundary by incorporating the contour information into the segmentation process. Our experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing liver segmentation methods in terms of accuracy and robustness. This method has the potential to assist radiologists in liver disease diagnosis and treatment planning.

Community detection is a fundamental problem in network analysis, with applications in various domains including social networks and biological networks. In this paper, we propose an unsupervised community detection method based on a Potts model Hamiltonian. We develop an efficient algorithm to solve the optimization problem associated with the Potts model, which allows us to detect communities in large-scale networks. We apply our method to digital pathology data, where the goal is to identify distinct regions within tissue samples. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in accurately detecting communities in both synthetic and real-world networks. Our method has the potential to significantly advance the field of digital pathology by enabling automated analysis of tissue samples.

This paper presents a novel approach to unsupervised community detection using a Potts model Hamiltonian. The proposed algorithm provides an efficient and scalable solution for identifying communities in complex networks. To validate the algorithm, it was applied to digital pathology images and demonstrated promising results in identifying distinct cellular communities within tissue samples. The proposed method has the potential to be widely applied in various fields where community detection is essential.

This paper presents a novel approach for robust submodular minimization, with applications to cooperative modeling. The proposed method leverages the concept of submodularity to efficiently solve optimization problems in cooperative modeling scenarios. The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach through extensive experiments on various datasets. The results show that the proposed method outperforms existing techniques in terms of both accuracy and efficiency. Overall, this paper contributes to the field of cooperative modeling by providing a robust and efficient solution for submodular minimization.

In this paper, we address the problem of robust submodular minimization, which is a fundamental task in machine learning and optimization. We propose a novel algorithm called RobustSM that incorporates both submodularity and robustness into the optimization process. We apply the RobustSM algorithm to cooperative modeling, a problem in which multiple agents collaborate to minimize a common objective function. Our experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of RobustSM in various cooperative modeling scenarios, including collaborative clustering and network influence maximization. Overall, our contributions advance the field of submodular optimization and provide practical solutions for cooperative modeling problems.

Deep learning-based segmentation methods have shown promising results in medical image analysis tasks. However, these methods typically require a large number of labeled atlases for training, which can be time-consuming and costly to obtain. In this paper, we propose a novel approach that demonstrates that only a few labeled atlases are necessary for accurate segmentation. We introduce a framework that combines a deep learning model with a transfer learning strategy to leverage the information from a small number of labeled atlases and a large number of unlabeled images. Our experiments on a dataset of brain MRI scans show that our approach achieves comparable segmentation performance to methods that use a larger number of labeled atlases. These findings suggest that our approach can significantly reduce the burden of obtaining labeled atlases for deep learning-based segmentation, making it more accessible and cost-effective for medical image analysis tasks.

This paper investigates the requirement of using a large number of labeled atlases for deep-learning-based segmentation tasks. The authors propose a novel deep learning framework that utilizes a small number of labeled atlases and synthesizes additional unlabeled atlases to train the model. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves competitive performance with a significantly reduced number of labeled atlases compared to traditional methods. This suggests that only a few labeled atlases are necessary for accurate segmentation using deep learning techniques, potentially saving significant time and effort in data annotation.

Efficient Video Semantic Segmentation with Labels Propagation and Refinement is an academic paper that proposes a novel approach for video semantic segmentation. The paper introduces a two-step process that combines label propagation and refinement techniques to improve the efficiency and accuracy of video segmentation. The first step involves propagating labels from keyframes to neighboring frames using a graph-based method. The second step refines the propagated labels using a convolutional neural network. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency. The paper concludes by discussing the potential applications and future directions of the proposed approach.

Efficient Video Semantic Segmentation with Labels Propagation and Refinement

Semantic segmentation is a challenging task in computer vision, especially in the context of videos where efficiency is crucial. In this paper, we propose an efficient approach for video semantic segmentation that combines label propagation and refinement techniques. We start by performing semantic segmentation on the first frame of the video using a deep learning model. Next, we propagate the labels from the first frame to the subsequent frames using optical flow information. This propagation process helps in leveraging temporal consistency and reducing computational costs. Additionally, we introduce a refinement stage where we further improve the segmentation result by applying a refinement network. This refinement network utilizes the propagated labels as input and produces a refined segmentation map. Experimental results on several video datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of our proposed approach compared to state-of-the-art methods.

Multi-focus image fusion is an important technique in image processing that aims to combine multiple images with different focus levels into a single image with enhanced overall focus. In this paper, we propose a novel multi-focus image fusion method based on similarity characteristics. The proposed method first calculates the similarity between each pixel in the input images using a similarity measure. Then, a weight map is generated based on the similarity values, which is used to assign weights to each pixel in the input images. Finally, the weighted average of the input images is computed to obtain the fused image. Experimental results on a dataset of multi-focus images demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of both visual quality and objective evaluation metrics. The proposed method is also computationally efficient, making it suitable for real-time applications.

Multi-focus image fusion is a key technology in image processing and computer vision that aims to obtain a fused image with both sharp foreground and background details from a set of input images taken at different focus settings. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for multi-focus image fusion based on similarity characteristics. The proposed method utilizes the similarity between pixel values in the input images to determine the importance of each pixel in the fused image. Specifically, we calculate the similarity measures between pixels in the input images and assign a weight to each pixel based on its similarity characteristics. We then perform a weighted average of the pixel values to obtain the fused image. Experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of visual quality and objective evaluation metrics. The proposed method is also computationally efficient, making it suitable for real-time applications.

This paper presents a novel method called OASIS (One-pass aligned Atlas Set) for image segmentation. The proposed method aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of image segmentation by aligning multiple atlases in a one-pass manner. The authors introduce a new alignment algorithm that aligns the atlases to a target image using a hierarchical registration strategy. The aligned atlases are then used to generate a segmentation map for the target image. Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate that the OASIS method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. The proposed method has the potential to be applied in various medical imaging applications, such as tumor detection and organ segmentation.

This paper presents OASIS, a novel one-pass aligned atlas set for image segmentation. Traditional atlas-based segmentation methods often require multiple iterations of registration, which can be time-consuming and computationally expensive. OASIS addresses this limitation by introducing a one-pass alignment process that efficiently registers a template atlas to a target image. This process involves two steps: a coarse alignment using a deep convolutional neural network, followed by a fine alignment using a robust multiresolution registration algorithm. Experimental results on various medical imaging datasets demonstrate that OASIS achieves competitive segmentation accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods, while significantly reducing computation time. Additionally, OASIS exhibits robustness against image artifacts and variations, making it suitable for a wide range of applications in medical imaging and beyond. Overall, this paper presents a new approach to atlas-based image segmentation that addresses the limitations of traditional methods, and offers improved speed, accuracy, and robustness.

This paper presents a novel approach for interactive 3D medical image segmentation using multi-agent reinforcement learning. The proposed method leverages the strengths of both human expertise and machine learning algorithms to achieve accurate and efficient segmentation results. The system consists of multiple agents, each responsible for a specific region of interest, and a human expert who provides initial guidance. The agents are trained using a combination of supervised learning and reinforcement learning, with an iterative refinement process to improve segmentation accuracy. Experimental results on a dataset of medical images demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, achieving superior segmentation performance compared to existing approaches. The proposed method has the potential to significantly improve the efficiency and accuracy of medical image segmentation, leading to better diagnosis and treatment planning in clinical practice.

Interactive 3D medical image segmentation is a challenging task due to the complexity and variability of medical data. In this paper, we propose an iteratively-refined interactive 3D medical image segmentation method using multi-agent reinforcement learning. Our method incorporates a deep Q-network (DQN) with the iterative refinement module to segment medical images interactively. The proposed method learns to optimize the interactive segmentation process through trial and error. We evaluate our method on three different medical image datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art interactive segmentation methods. The experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves significant improvements in segmentation accuracy and efficiency. Furthermore, the proposed method also shows the ability to generalize to new datasets with high performance. Overall, this paper presents a promising approach for interactive 3D medical image segmentation using multi-agent reinforcement learning.

This paper presents an approach for adaptive automatic threat recognition within 3D computed tomography (CT) images for baggage security screening. The proposed approach utilizes a deep learning framework to automatically detect and classify potential threats within CT images. The framework is trained on a large dataset of annotated CT images, allowing it to learn and recognize various types of threats. Additionally, the approach incorporates an adaptive learning mechanism that continuously updates the model based on new data, improving its performance over time. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, achieving high accuracy in threat detection and classification. The adaptive nature of the approach also allows it to adapt to new and emerging threats, making it a valuable tool for enhancing baggage security screening systems.

This paper presents an approach for adaptive automatic threat recognition within 3D computed tomography (CT) images for baggage security screening. Baggage security screening plays a crucial role in ensuring the safety of air travel. While manual screening methods are currently used, they are time-consuming and prone to errors. To improve the efficiency and accuracy of baggage screening, automated methods based on CT imaging have been developed. However, these methods often struggle with detecting rare or novel threats and suffer from high false alarm rates. In this paper, we propose an adaptive approach that combines deep learning techniques with transfer learning and anomaly detection to address these challenges. The proposed method is capable of recognizing known threats with high accuracy and can also identify previously unseen threats. We evaluate our approach on a large dataset of 3D CT images and compare its performance to existing methods. The results demonstrate that our adaptive approach outperforms conventional methods, achieving higher detection rates with lower false alarm rates. This work provides a promising solution for improving the effectiveness of baggage security screening and enhancing aviation safety.

QANet is a novel quality assurance network designed specifically for image segmentation tasks. Image segmentation is a critical step in many computer vision applications, and ensuring the accuracy and reliability of the segmentation results is of utmost importance. QANet addresses this challenge by leveraging a deep neural network architecture that combines both local and global information to generate high-quality segmentation masks. The network is trained using a large dataset of annotated images and achieves state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets. Additionally, QANet incorporates a novel quality assessment module that provides a quantitative measure of the segmentation quality, enabling users to evaluate and compare different segmentation algorithms. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of QANet in improving the quality of image segmentation results.

QANet is presented as a novel quality assurance network for image segmentation tasks. The proposed framework leverages the use of deep neural networks to generate high-quality segmentations by incorporating both global and local context information. The network architecture is designed to address the unique challenges faced in image segmentation, such as class imbalance and object occlusion. Additionally, QANet incorporates a novel quality assessment mechanism that allows for the selection of the most reliable segmentation outputs. Extensive experiments on various benchmark datasets demonstrate the superior performance of QANet compared to existing state-of-the-art methods. The results suggest that QANet is a promising approach for improving the quality and accuracy of image segmentation tasks.

Semantic image segmentation is a challenging task that requires pixel-level labeling of objects in an image. Weakly supervised semantic image segmentation, where only image-level labels are available, is even more challenging. In this paper, we propose a novel loss function called Gated CRF Loss for weakly supervised semantic image segmentation. The Gated CRF Loss combines the advantages of Conditional Random Fields (CRF) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) by incorporating a gating mechanism. This gating mechanism allows the model to selectively apply the CRF loss based on the confidence of the CNN predictions. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our proposed Gated CRF Loss outperforms existing weakly supervised semantic image segmentation methods, achieving state-of-the-art performance. Furthermore, we provide an ablation study to analyze the effectiveness of the different components of our proposed loss function. Overall, our work contributes to the field of weakly supervised semantic image segmentation by introducing a novel loss function that improves the accuracy of the segmentation results.

This paper introduces a novel loss function for weakly supervised semantic image segmentation using a Gated Conditional Random Field (CRF) approach. The proposed loss function aims to improve the accuracy and consistency of the segmentation by incorporating both pixel-level and global contextual information. The Gated CRF mechanism acts as a gate to selectively combine the two sources of information, allowing for more accurate and precise pixel labeling. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed loss function in achieving state-of-the-art performance in weakly supervised semantic image segmentation tasks.

This paper presents a novel approach for liver segmentation using a deeply self-supervised contour embedded neural network. Liver segmentation is a crucial step in medical image analysis and plays a vital role in various clinical applications. The proposed method leverages the power of deep learning and self-supervised learning to accurately segment the liver from abdominal CT scans. The contour embedding technique is employed to capture the fine details and boundaries of the liver, enhancing the segmentation performance. Extensive experiments on a large dataset demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method, achieving state-of-the-art results in liver segmentation. The proposed approach has the potential to significantly improve the accuracy and efficiency of liver segmentation in clinical practice, leading to better diagnosis and treatment planning.

This paper presents a novel approach for liver segmentation using a deep neural network architecture that incorporates contour embeddings through self-supervised learning. The proposed method leverages a deeply self-supervised learning framework that utilizes unlabeled data to learn useful contour embeddings for accurate liver segmentation. The network architecture is designed to incorporate shape priors by learning from the inherent structure of the data itself. Experimental results on a publicly available liver segmentation dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method compared to other state-of-the-art segmentation algorithms. This work highlights the potential of contour embedding and self-supervised learning for improving medical image segmentation tasks.

This paper presents a novel approach for post-mortem iris recognition using deep-learning-based image segmentation. The proposed method aims to address the challenges posed by post-mortem iris images, such as degradation and discoloration. The authors propose a deep learning architecture that combines a convolutional neural network (CNN) with a U-Net for accurate and robust iris segmentation. The CNN is trained on a large dataset of post-mortem iris images, and the U-Net is used to refine the segmentation results. Experimental results on a benchmark dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, achieving high segmentation accuracy and improved iris recognition performance compared to existing methods. The proposed approach has the potential to enhance the reliability and applicability of iris recognition in forensic investigations and other post-mortem scenarios.

This paper presents a method for post-mortem iris recognition using deep-learning-based image segmentation. Post-mortem iris recognition is a challenging task due to various factors that affect the quality and appearance of the iris after death. The proposed method utilizes a deep convolutional neural network to automatically segment the iris region from post-mortem iris images. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, achieving high segmentation accuracy even in challenging scenarios. The segmented iris regions are then used for iris recognition, using a state-of-the-art iris recognition algorithm. The proposed method achieves promising results in post-mortem iris recognition, providing a potential solution for forensic applications.

TFLMS: Large Model Support in TensorFlow by Graph Rewriting

Abstract:

Deep learning models have become increasingly complex and require large amounts of memory to train and deploy. However, existing deep learning frameworks like TensorFlow have limitations in handling large models due to memory constraints. In this paper, we propose TFLMS, a novel approach to address this issue by introducing large model support in TensorFlow through graph rewriting. TFLMS leverages the concept of graph rewriting to dynamically allocate and deallocate memory for model parameters, allowing for efficient training and deployment of large models. We demonstrate the effectiveness of TFLMS through experiments on various deep learning tasks, including image classification and natural language processing. Our results show that TFLMS significantly reduces memory usage and improves training and inference performance compared to existing approaches. Furthermore, TFLMS is compatible with existing TensorFlow models and can be easily integrated into the TensorFlow ecosystem. Overall, TFLMS provides a practical solution for handling large models in TensorFlow, enabling researchers and practitioners to train and deploy complex deep learning models more efficiently.

TFLMS: Large Model Support in TensorFlow by Graph Rewriting

This paper introduces TFLMS, an approach to support large models in TensorFlow through graph rewriting techniques. Large models, especially those with deep neural network architectures, often encounter memory limitations during training and inference. TFLMS addresses this challenge by introducing novel strategies to optimize memory usage and accelerate the execution of TensorFlow graphs.

The authors present a comprehensive analysis of the memory bottlenecks in TensorFlow and propose a set of graph rewriting rules to overcome these limitations. These rules leverage the unique characteristics of deep neural networks and adapt the graph representation to enable efficient operations on subgraphs.

TFLMS also introduces a memory-efficient parallel execution strategy for TensorFlow graphs, enabling models to scale across multiple GPUs. By applying graph rewriting techniques, TFLMS reduces the memory footprint of large models, allowing them to fit into the available GPU memory and leading to significant speedups in both training and inference.

The authors provide an extensive evaluation of TFLMS on a variety of benchmarks, demonstrating its effectiveness in reducing memory usage and improving performance for large models. They also compare TFLMS with other existing approaches and discuss its advantages and limitations.

Overall, this paper presents a novel approach, TFLMS, which addresses the memory limitations of large models in TensorFlow. The proposed graph rewriting techniques offer a promising solution to optimize memory usage and accelerate the execution of deep neural networks, enabling researchers and practitioners to train and deploy larger and more complex models.
